entries.title: Differentiating Through Linear Solvers

detail.title: Differentiating Through Linear Solvers
evidence: Both arXiv abstract records list Paul Hovland then Jan Hückelheim; both PDFs and HTML bodies list Jan then Paul with equal contribution. The manuscript follows the abstract record, so its order cannot fairly be called a confirmed error.
The v1 PDF contains an ICML 2023 / PMLR 202 template footer, removed in v2. It is not evidence of publication in those proceedings; the cited arXiv 2024 status is appropriate.
Studies low-level differentiation through GMRES, TFQMR and BiCGStab versus equation-level differentiation on 65 SuiteSparse matrices; primarily forward mode.
detail.manuscript_use: Line 95 supports the warning that forward agreement does not establish derivative agreement; lines 464–465 explicitly describe implementation-versus-equation differentiation, primarily forward mode.
detail.support_assessment: Accurate description in related work; valid conceptual precedent for separating solution and derivative accuracy.
detail.boundary: Not an experiment on FP32 versus FP64 Cholesky stages, restored Adam/AdamW updates, or long-horizon learned-ridge training. Treating it as direct evidence for those details would overextend it.
issues: Source-internal author order discrepancy. Recommend a version-specific link or note if exact author order needs resolution; do not penalize the manuscript solely for following arXiv metadata.

entries.title: A taxonomy of automatic differentiation pitfalls

detail.title: A taxonomy of automatic differentiation pitfalls
detail.venue: WIREs Data Mining and Knowledge Discovery
evidence: Publisher lists these six authors in this order, first publication 2 September 2024, issue November/December 2024, 14(6):e1555.

detail.manuscript_use: Lines 457–458 group higher-precision accumulation, master weights, loss scaling and tensor assignment precedents.

detail.boundary: The BFLOAT16 paper emphasizes avoiding additional hyperparameter changes in its experiments; loss scaling in the grouped sentence is most directly associated with FP16 work such as Micikevicius. No citation mismatch established.
